scope: Identity-masked comparison of the earth clause under exactly retained WLC consonants, pointing and segmentation. Not a source-priority or whole-verse optimum decision.
source_text: הָרִים֙ רָעֲשׁ֣וּ מִמֶּ֔/נּוּ וְ/הַ/גְּבָע֖וֹת הִתְמֹגָ֑גוּ וַ/תִּשָּׂ֤א הָ/אָ֨רֶץ֙ מִ/פָּנָ֔י/ו וְ/תֵבֵ֖ל וְ/כָל יֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽ/הּ־׃
close_gloss: Mountains quake from/because of him; the hills dissolve; and the earth lifts/rises from/before his face, the inhabited world and all its inhabitants. The unusual intransitive verb use makes this a diagnostic gloss, not a settled sense.
context_before: He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither; even the blossom of Lebanon withers.
context_after: Who can stand before his indignation? And who can rise up in the heat of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered by him.

candidates.K: The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away; the earth heaves before him, the world and all who dwell in it.
candidates.R: The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away; the earth rises up before his face, the world and all who dwell in it.

policy.priority: Meaning and unsupported additions first; ambiguity, literary effect, naturalness and consistency next. Readability serves fidelity.
policy.preserve: Cosmic scope; the earth/world/inhabitants parallelism; do not soften divine judgment or require a literal geology claim.
policy.face_idiom: Evaluate natural referential English separately from the anthropomorphic lexical image. Either candidate may be footnoted for lost nuance.
policy.chronology: No older-witness weighting decides an English choice against unchanged source.

evidence_limits: The completed full-article review found no decisive new Hebrew letters or ancient vowel points for the earth verb. The Greek passive does not require a Hebrew Niphal of נשׂא.

The Greek fragment's preferred simplex verb is not wholly secured against possible compounds; lifting/removal/shaking/devastation renderings can reflect interpretive translation rather than distinct Hebrew spellings.

The retained pointing is analyzed as נשׂא, with unusual intransitive usage. Poetic usage and cited related-language comparisons are counter-explanations to emendation; cited lexicon entries were not independently inspected.

Repointing the same consonants as an apocopated Niphal of שׁאה is a serious alternative. It is outside this same-pointing application and should remain disclosed, not silently encoded in either candidate.
A more natural English presence expression does not uniquely establish a different Hebrew preposition. Literal face wording can be disclosed in a note.
This assessment tests English tradeoffs under the declared interpretation, not historical priority or a unique optimal translation.
rubric: Meaning and grammatical agency under retained pointing
Unsupported direction, destruction, or anthropomorphic constraints
Preserved ambiguity and lost nuance with an explicit counterargument
Whether the change is worth applying, retaining or holding; one assessment only
requested_result: Assess each candidate by rubric, state your working preference or HOLD and strongest objection, then check whether reversed order changes your reasoning. Do not assign numerical truth probabilities.
